transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: uh good afternoon thank you for calling S-Net fibre technical support owen speaking how can i help you out today mate

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Owen, my name is Dashiell. My full fibre broadband suddenly died about forty minutes ago while I was on a video call, and the little white ONT box on the wall is flashing red on the LOS light.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: ah mate i'm really sorry you've been knocked offline right in the middle of your workday i completely understand how frustrating and stressful that is when a video call drops out

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Owen. Yeah, it's Dashiell—D-A-S-H-I-E-L-L—on account 904-2281. I've got landscaping contractors out in the front garden today digging near the boundary wall, so I'm dreading that they've nicked something.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: no worries pal let's get you passed security first uh can you confirm the first line of your address and your four digit account PIN for me

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, the address is 12B Broomhall Road, Sheffield, S10 2DR, and the PIN is 6104.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: spot on mate 12B Broomhall Road and PIN 6104 are both verified on the system here

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great. So around 11:15 AM the internet completely died, and when I walked over to the hallway cupboard, the Nokia ONT box had a flashing red light next to LOS.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: gotcha pal so just to put it in my own words since your landscapers were digging near the front boundary wall around 11:15 this morning your indoor Nokia ONT has had a flashing red LOS light and your Hub 4 has lost all internet connection

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yep, that's bang on. The Hub 4 router itself has a pulsing orange globe light, and the Nokia box next to it has the flashing red LOS LED.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: right mate let's do a quick check of all four LEDs on that indoor Nokia ONT box uh looking from left to right what are the Power PON LOS and LAN lights doing right now

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Looking at the Nokia box right now: the Power light is solid green, the PON light is completely off, the LOS light is flashing bright red, and the LAN1 light is flickering green where the ethernet cable goes to the Hub 4.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: okay solid green Power PON totally dark and LOS flashing red definitely means zero optical laser signal reaching the photodiode inside your ONT mate

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Before we blame the guys with the mini-digger outside, is there anything inside the cupboard I should check on the white cable?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: good thinking pal uh trace the thin white optical patch lead coming out of the bottom of the Nokia ONT with the green SC APC plug has anything in the cupboard pushed against it or bent it sharply

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me open the cupboard door wider... no, the white fibre lead goes straight from the green plug at the bottom of the ONT into the little white wall splice socket, untouched.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: and is the green SC APC connector clicked all the way flush into the bottom optical port on the ONT mate no dust cap loose or anything

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm gently pressing the green collar upwards right now—it's clicked in solid, didn't budge a millimetre, and the red LOS light is still flashing away.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: right pal let's power cycle the ONT transceiver just in case the laser receiver latched into protection mode uh can you flick the little black rocker button on the side of the Nokia ONT off for ten seconds

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I've pressed the black rocker switch off—all the lights on the Nokia ONT are dark now. Counting ten seconds...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: sound mate give it another three or four seconds and then pop that rocker switch back in

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Just clicked it back on. The Power light is green... waiting for PON... nope, PON stayed off and LOS has gone straight back to flashing red.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: yeah i thought it might mate now tell me a bit more about what the landscapers were doing outside around 11:15 AM near your front boundary wall

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They're taking out a row of old laurel bushes right next to the driveway entrance and using a compact mini-digger to trench about forty centimetres deep for new granite edging stones.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: forty centimetres deep right by the laurel bushes near the driveway entrance uh do you know where the grey external S-Net Customer Splice Point box sits on your outside brickwork mate

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! The grey S-Net CSP box is mounted on the side wall right behind where the second laurel bush was! The black micro-duct comes up out of the soil along that exact wall.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: ah right behind the second laurel bush where the black micro-duct comes up out of the soil hang on a sec while i run an optical time-domain reflectometer test from the Sheffield exchange OLT

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, go ahead and run the test.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: right mate that optical trace from our Sheffield OLT has come back showing complete loss of reflection at 318 metres from the splitter cabinet which is right at the boundary of 12B Broomhall Road

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh no—so 318 metres from the cabinet means the break is right here on my property boundary where they were trenching at 11:15?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: spot on pal the OLT sees normal backscatter all the way to the pavement Toby box outside your driveway and then total open circuit between the Toby box and your grey CSP on the wall

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, could the mini-digger bucket have crushed or snapped the black sub-duct underground between the pavement Toby box and the wall?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: almost certainly mate when S-Net installs full fibre across a garden or driveway the purple or black 14-millimetre sub-duct is usually buried about 25 to 35 centimetres down

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And my landscapers were trenching 40 centimetres deep to lay the concrete bed for the granite edging stones!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: yeah pal if they went 40 centimetres down where the sub-duct sits at 30 centimetres that digger bucket will have gone straight through the blown fibre tube

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you walk outside with me while I'm on my mobile and tell me what to look for in the trench next to the grey CSP box?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: course i can mate take your phone out to the front garden and tell me what you can see in the trench underneath the grey CSP box on the brickwork

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm walking out the front door now... okay, I'm standing by the trench where the second laurel bush was pulled out. Looking down into the soil...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: can you see a black or purple plastic tube about the thickness of a garden hose coming out of the earth toward the grey wall box mate

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh blimey—yes! There's a black plastic tube sticking out of the soil, and it's flattened and torn open with tiny hair-like glass fibres frayed out of a yellow sleeve!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: oof yeah torn black sub-duct with frayed glass fibres in a yellow sleeve means the 2-fibre drop cable is completely severed mate wait there while i check the duct map and civils records

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'm still here by the driveway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: okay looking at the GIS plant map here the underground feed from the pavement Toby box across your driveway and laurel bed was laid as an armoured sub-duct by our external civils contractor

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so how quickly can you book an S-Net engineer and a civils crew to replace the crushed duct and re-blow the fibre cable into the grey box?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: well mate i can log a standard overhead or wall-box splice fault on my screen for an S-Net fibre engineer to visit on Friday morning between 8 AM and 1 PM

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, Friday morning 8 AM to 1 PM for the fibre splice engineer—what about repairing the crushed underground sub-duct between the pavement Toby box and my wall so the engineer can actually pull the new cable through?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: uh if the armoured sub-duct under your driveway and laurel bed is crushed that's between you and our external civils contractor Kelly Group—you'll have to ring their regional depot yourself to sort out re-laying the cable duct

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, what?! Why would I have to ring Kelly Group's regional depot myself?! My contract is with S-Net, not Kelly Group!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: yeah i hear you mate but here on the technical desk my system only books the internal S-Net splice van it doesn't let me dispatch a Kelly Group two-man civils digging crew

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Surely S-Net has an internal civils coordination team or a way for you to book the Kelly Group duct crew on the same ticket?! If I ring Kelly Group as a member of the public, they won't even talk to me without an S-Net work order!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: look pal they have a Yorkshire regional office in Rotherham if you google Kelly Group Rotherham depot and tell them your address at 12B Broomhall Road has a crushed S-Net micro-duct they can tell you when their groundworks lads are in S10

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Owen, you've been super friendly on the phone, bit telling me to google your subcontractor's Rotherham depot and arrange my own underground duct repair is crazy!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: i'm really sorry about the hassle mate i know it's a proper pain when two different teams are involved

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So if the S-Net splice engineer turns up on Friday morning between 8 AM and 1 PM and the black sub-duct in the trench is still pinched shut five feet from the Toby box, what happens?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: if the S-Net engineer can't rod a new drop fibre through the existing tube on Friday mate they'll either clip a temporary surface cable along the top of your boundary wall or mark the job as needing civils

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait—if I ask my landscapers right now to leave the trench open so the crushed section of black tube is completely exposed and accessible, can the Friday engineer coupler a new piece of sub-duct onto it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: actually mate that's a massive shout if your landscapers leave that trench uncovered where the black 14-millimetre tube is torn the S-Net engineer carries push-fit straight connectors in the van

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Really? So if the trench is still open and the two clean ends of the black plastic duct are exposed, the engineer can cut out the crushed foot of pipe and push-fit a coupler?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: 100 percent pal as long as the tube isn't crushed further back under the tarmac towards the pavement Toby box a push-fit 14-millimetre coupler lets them blow a fresh fibre straight from the Toby box to your grey CSP

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me shout to the foreman right now not to backfill that corner by the second laurel bush! Hold on two seconds... okay, I've told him to leave that metre of trench open until Friday afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: brilliant mate i've put a note on the engineer job sheet saying the customer has left the trench open at the second laurel bush behind the grey CSP box and the 2-fibre yellow drop is severed at 318 metres

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the job reference number for Friday morning's appointment, Owen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: your engineer appointment reference is FLT-7739204 booked for Friday between 08:00 and 13:00 at 12B Broomhall Road mate

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: FLT-7739204. Now, what am I supposed to do for internet between now and Friday afternoon? I work from home full-time as a software architect.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: do you have an S-Net mobile SIM with us pal or are you on another mobile network

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've got an S-Net 10 gigabyte monthly SIM in my iPhone, which is what I'm talking to you on right now, and my wife also has an S-Net SIM.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: ah wicked mate because your SIM is on the same S-Net account 904-2281 i can load an unlimited 5G data boost onto both your iPhone SIM and your wife's SIM for the next seven days free of charge

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that actually helps a ton! If I've got unlimited 5G data on my iPhone, I can tether my MacBook Pro to my personal hotspot until the fibre is spliced on Friday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: i've just activated the seven-day unlimited data pass on both mobile numbers on your account mate you'll get a confirmation text in about thirty seconds

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The text message just popped up on my screen: 'Your 7-day Unlimited Data Boost is now active.' Thanks for sorting that part out, Owen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: pleasure pal and should i leave your indoor Nokia ONT switched on or switched off while the bare glass fibres are sticking out in the garden trench

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good question—is there any laser safety hazard with the broken fibre in the trench?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: the OLT laser from the exchange shuts down automatically under automatic laser shutdown when the loop breaks mate but it's still best practice to switch off the indoor Nokia ONT at the plug and wrap a bit of electrical tape over the frayed cable end outside so nobody pricks a finger on the glass shards

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good advice, I'll wrap some PVC electrical tape around the frayed end in the trench and switch off the Nokia ONT power socket inside until Friday morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: top man so right now your fibre broadband connection itself is obviously still down with the red LOS light until the field splice engineer arrives on Friday morning under reference FLT-7739204

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, the fibre is still dead, though at least I've got the unlimited 5G hotspot to keep me working until Friday morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: awesome mate is there anything else i can check for you today before we wrap up

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything for now, Owen. Cheers.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: no worries at all pal thank you for choosing S-Net and good luck with the rest of the garden landscaping cheers bye

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Cheers Owen, bye.
